expected-results.json in the VS Code repository, which was generated from a
Every entry must state the Eclipse engine's actual normalized smell list and
the reason for the difference. The corpus runner fails if a case diverges
without an entry here, and also fails if an entry no longer diverges, so this
file cannot drift away from reality.

notComparedFields.testMethods: The engine in this repository does not report a test-method count. The newer engine emits a NumberOfMethods column; this one has no equivalent, so the field is recorded in the manifest but not compared on the Eclipse side.

divergences.reason: Magic Number Test. The test contains no assertion at all. This engine raises the smell only when an assertion argument is a numeric literal, so it reports nothing; the newer engine reports the smell regardless.
Magic Number Test. Both assertions compare string literals. This engine counts only numeric literals as magic numbers.
Magic Number Test. The single assertion compares string literals. This engine counts only numeric literals as magic numbers.
Magic Number Test. assertTrue is called with a boolean expression and a string argument, with no numeric literal present.
